title: 3D Cloth Simulation (Verlet Integration + Wind Force)
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a 3D cloth simulation that simulates a piece of cloth suspended from two fixed points and fluttering in the wind.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>

[Cloth Physics Model (Mass-Spring System + Verlet Integration)]
Cloth grid: 25×25 = 625 particles, initially laid flat on the xz plane (y=5), with spacing restLength = 0.2m
Total cloth dimensions are approximately 4.8m × 4.8m

Fixed points: The two particles at the upper-left corner (0, 5, 0) and upper-right corner (4.8, 5, 0) remain fixed in place

Spring constraints (3 types):
- Structural springs (Structural): Connect adjacent particles (up, down, left, and right), restLength = 0.2
- Shear springs (Shear): Connect diagonally adjacent particles, restLength = 0.2√2 ≈ 0.283
- Bending springs (Bending): Connect particles separated by one intermediate particle, restLength = 0.4

Time integration: Verlet Integration
  x_new = x + (x - x_prev) * damping + acceleration * dt²
  damping = 0.99
  dt = 0.016 (60fps)

Constraint solving: Perform 15 constraint relaxation iterations per frame
  For each spring, pull the two endpoint particles back toward restLength:
  correction = (distance - restLength) / distance * 0.5 * direction
  p1 += correction, p2 -= correction (fixed points do not move)
  If distance > restLength * 1.5, the spring breaks (optional, but earns bonus credit)

External forces:
- Gravity: (0, -9.81, 0) m/s²
- Wind force: Periodically varying wind F_wind = windStrength * sin(time * 0.5) * (0, 0, 1)
  windStrength can be adjusted using a slider, with a range of 0-20 and a default value of 5

Collision: A sphere is located below the cloth at y=0 (radius 1.0, centered at (2.4, 1.5, 0)); if a cloth particle enters the sphere, push it to the sphere's surface

Perform 3 physics sub-steps per frame to ensure stability.

[Rendering]
(1) Render the cloth using THREE.Mesh + PlaneGeometry, updating vertex positions and normals every frame
(2) Double-sided material (DoubleSide), with a white front side and a light gray back side
(3) Collision sphere: translucent red sphere
(4) Mark the two fixed points with small yellow spheres
(5) OrbitControls + directional light + ambient light

[HUD and Controls]
(6) HUD (IDs as follows):
  - Particle count (id="nodeCount")
  - Average stretch ratio (id="avgStretch"): the average of |current length/restLength - 1| across all springs
  - Maximum stretch ratio (id="maxStretch")
  - Simulation time (id="simTime")

(7) Wind force slider (id="windSlider", range 0-20, default 5)
(8) Reset button (id="resetBtn")

[State Exposure]
(9) Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame, containing:
  - nodeCount: particle count (625)
  - pinned: array of fixed points [{x,y,z}]
  - avgStretch: average stretch ratio
  - maxStretch: maximum stretch ratio
  - simTime: simulation time
  - windStrength: current wind force value
  - centerOfMass: {x,y,z} cloth center of mass
  - lowestY: y coordinate of the lowest point of the cloth
  - nodes: sampled array (take one out of every 5, ~125 points), each item is {x,y,z}
  - springCount: total number of springs
  - brokenSprings: number of broken springs

Output a single standalone HTML file.
physics_constraints: Average stretch should be < 5% at rest (constraint solver quality)
